lines.trans: Nagiyev and she, they were here!
Dima is the last train car for me.
Why, you drank too much, brother.
Alright, enough, go and sleep it off.
And here I am running around looking for you.
I could not understand where you disappeared to.

words.gram: future, 1st person singular, perfective (idiomatic for 'I can't understand')

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе, и прости меня за все.
examples.trans: Thank you, and forgive me for everything.
And you forgive me too.
Excuse me, where is he?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where is Louis?
Misha, where is the pianist?
Well where are they?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Замуж она выходит не в моем кабинете.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: Maybe he left on his own?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: Did you want to see me?
Hello, glad to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is for my niece.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last').

examples.text: Я надеюсь, это в последний раз, когда готовят свадебные печеньки.
examples.trans: I hope this is the last time wedding cookies are made for you.

examples.text: И Дима для меня последний вагон.
examples.trans: And Dima is the last train car for me.
My bald last train car.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the very').

examples.text: Я читал сам про это дело.
examples.trans: I read about this matter myself.

examples.text: Ты сама взяла и уволила Дениса.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частливый'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('happy').

examples.trans: Nothing, I am very happy.

examples.text: Веришь, я на самом деле счастлива.

meanings.en: to overstep the mark, go too far
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'drank too much'.

examples.trans: Why, you drank too much, brother.
You have really overstepped now, Major.

examples.text: Ты сейчас сильно перебрал, майор Лавров!
examples.trans: You have really overstepped now, Major Lavrov!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'brother' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Surely you would be glad about that.
The marriage fell apart—the mother-in-law is to blame.
Why, you drank too much, brother.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enough', paired with 'хватать'.

meanings.en: to sleep off drunkenness, sober up through sleep
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'спаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sleep it off', paired with 'просыпаться'.

examples.trans: Go home and sleep it off properly.
In the morning he finally slept it off.
Enough making noise, go sleep it off, commander.

examples.trans: Let's go through the wedding script.

meanings.en: to vanish, disappear, get away (куда денется = where can one go)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go, vanish, disappear'.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

meanings.en: to rest, to take a break
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дыхать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'rest, relax', paired with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.trans: Go rest, Misha.

examples.text: Вы отдыхайте, а мы сами поедем.
examples.trans: You rest, and we'll go ourselves.
